title: Obscurity Blamed on the Writer
core: All six say the same thing: I could not follow this, and that is your fault. None is neutral — each carries an implied accusation that the difficulty was avoidable, that a clearer version existed and wasn't written. What separates them is *what the difficulty is made of* — depth, murk, knots, detours, institutional sprawl — and *how much intent* the speaker is willing to allege, from mild suspicion up to flat charge of bad faith.

words.nuance: The only one where the difficulty is genuinely in the *content*: the ideas are deep and specialist, and the prose may be perfectly straight. Blame here is a raised eyebrow, not a charge — the speaker suspects plainer treatment was possible but concedes the subject really is hard.

Murk, not shape. Nothing is tangled or knotted — it's simply opaque, sediment stirred up so you can't see through. It's also the only one with a live technical literal sense (water samples, river surveys), which is why applying it to prose stings: you clouded a thing that would have settled clear on its own.

Knots. The parts are folded back on each other so you lose the thread — you can't tell what depends on what. Where turbid prose is opaque, convoluted prose is legible sentence by sentence and incomprehensible as a whole.

Detour, not knot. It *does* arrive — by way of everywhere else. The complaint is length and indirection, so it fits a negotiation, a chain of reasoning, or a road; and unlike convoluted's tangle, the parts stay in order, there are just far too many of them.

Reserve it for *systems* — tax codes, bureaucracies, permit processes, org charts — never for a single sentence. It adds scale and an inside: the intricacy is old, accreted, and profits whoever already knows the channels.

The only verb, so it's the only one that names an agent and pins intent — the others describe a result that might be incompetence. And its method is addition: you obfuscate by piling jargon, clauses, and caveats on top of a fact, not by omitting it.

exam_note: Every word here is negative, so tone gets you nowhere — the answer turns on what the obscurity is made of (depth / murk / knots / detours / institutions) and whether the sentence blames a person, which only **obfuscate** does outright; also watch the **tortuous**/*torturous* swap, which is about twisting, not pain.
